candidate_relations.reason: The clinical scenario—prior PE tube insertion, subsequent polypoid mass with purulent discharge, erosive skull base changes, and intracranial extension—is consistent with an aggressive granulomatous reaction to a retained foreign body (the PE tube). The reference diagnosis of foreign body granuloma is a specific benign etiology. C001 asserts a malignant neoplasm, which is an incompatible diagnostic category even though the imaging findings (erosion, intracranial extension) could superficially suggest malignancy. The two diagnoses are mutually exclusive in etiology and management.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: C001 asserts primary malignancy (cancer) of the middle ear with skull base and intracranial extension; the reference diagnosis is foreign body granuloma, a benign reactive/inflammatory process

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis (foreign body granuloma) is atypical for the degree of skull base erosion and intracranial extension described; histopathologic confirmation would normally be required to distinguish from malignancy or cholesteatoma in this clinical context.
Profound sensorineural hearing loss is unusual for a purely middle ear/mastoid foreign body granuloma and may warrant additional scrutiny of the reference diagnosis.
